rationale: First-index argmax selects background 0, 4-connectivity, and largest pixel count. Separated solid rectangles make both connectivities equivalent and largest count equivalent to largest bounding box.
Select the smallest object on background 0. Separated solid rectangles give identical components under both connectivities, and smallest pixel count also selects the smallest bounding box.

For separated solid rectangles, largest pixel count equals largest bounding-box area under either connectivity. First-index argmax implements this with no nonzero weights and also covers largest-count patterns.
For separated solid rectangles, smallest pixel count equals smallest bounding-box area under either connectivity, also covering smallest-count patterns.
Crop the topmost object on background 0. Both connectivities identify the same separated rectangles; only the selection criterion requires a nonzero weight.
Crop the object with the lowest bottom edge on background 0. Both connectivities identify the same separated rectangles; only the selection criterion requires a nonzero weight.
